messages:
anna: Quick sync — thinking about a role-graph compactification migration. Idea: store a tight per-actor bitmask (roles) + an exceptions list per-resource. Pros: much smaller token size, faster checks in hot path. Cons: loses some human-readable semantics and makes introspection harder. anyone see a blocker?

vikram: i like the runtime perf win but worried about admin/console UX. how do we map bits back to meaningful roles?

maya: can we keep the verbose model for the console and mint compact tokens for runtime? compile verbose -> compact when issuing tokens.

ryan: that seems reasonable. migration story matters though — old tokens will still be in the wild, need dual support.

sam: +1. also we need stable claim names. proposal: use 'r' for role-bitset (int) and 'rx' for exceptions (array of strings). example payload: {
  "sub": "svc-ingest",
  "r": 42,
  "rx": ["project:123:deny.write"]
}

anna: exactly. runtime pseudocode: if token.r then eval bitset else eval verboseRoles. question: where do we do legacy->compact conversion? at mint time for persistent tokens or at proxy-ingress on the fly?

vikram: prefer conversion at authn proxy (ingress) so internal services don't need to change. one place to convert = less runtime churn.

maya: ops: conversion at proxy adds latency and complexity. require metrics + circuit-breaker flag. also need to rate-limit heavy conversions.

security-bot: NOTE: any new claim keys must be registered with token-claims audit and KMS rotation teams. See policy: https://internal.redwood/policy/token-claims

ryan: UI note — console must never show raw bitsets. keep a server-side mapping table (bit->friendly role name) and render friendly names. store mapping with versioning.

sam: rollout plan sketch:
1) Mint compact by default for NEW tokens under feature-flag.
2) Implement runtime dual-parse (r + verbose) for 9 months.
3) Provide a conversion tool + bulk rewrite for long-lived tokens.
4) Audit + deprecate verbose claim after migration window.

maya: security wants a shorter deprecation window (6 months). ops pushes back.

vikram: operational reality says 9 months minimum to reach external integrators. propose compromise: 6 months for internal tokens, 9 months for external.

anna: agreed. decisions to capture in RFC follow-up: compact tokens for runtime; verbose model retained for UX; conversion performed at proxy; runtime supports dual-parse; console maps bitsets to names server-side with versioning; deprecation windows: internal 6mo, external 9mo. I'll open the RFC follow-up and assign action items (conversion tool, metrics dashboard, mapping table schema). :thumbsup:
